text.content:
Spellcasting in Arneyan

Magic in the wilds of Veradyna is a test of will and focus. We use a flexible system that combines the tactical choices of modern editions with the high-stakes risk of the old school.

Magic is resolved based on whether a spell harms, debuffs, or simply does something useful.

Saving Throws

  • When: used for any spell that damages or debuffs a target (e.g. Fireball, Hold Person, Fear, Ray of Enfeeblement, Blindness/Deafness)
  • The Spell DC: the universal formula is roll-over: DC = 10 + half your caster level (rounded down, minimum 1; your caster level is your Class Level in that class, which for a single-class character is your character level) + your casting-stat modifier. A caster's DC is the same whichever spell they cast, regardless of spell level
  • Resolving: the target rolls d20 + the matching save (Fortitude/Reflex/Will, whichever the spell calls for) + half the target's level (rounded down, minimum 1), and succeeds if the total meets or beats the DC
  • The Defence: Fortitude = Constitution modifier, Reflex = Dexterity modifier, Will = Wisdom modifier (Strength, Intelligence, and Charisma don't feed a save directly)
  • Advantage/Disadvantage: apply as normal (GM discretion, or situational/manoeuvre rules). A natural 20 always succeeds the save; a natural 1 always fails it, regardless of the total — same convention as attack rolls
  • Concentration: spells marked (concentration) last only while you keep focus. Only one at a time; it ends if you take damage and fail the Fortitude save, are Stunned, Paralysed or Unconscious, or cast another concentration spell (see Concentration in Section II of the Codex).
  • Worked Example: a 6th-level Cleric (Wisdom 16, +2 modifier) casts Hold Person at a bandit. DC = 10 + half her level (6 ÷ 2 = 3) + 2 = 15. The bandit (Wisdom 13, +1 modifier, 3rd-level) rolls d20 + 1 (Wisdom modifier) + half its level (3 ÷ 2, rounded down to 1) = d20 + 2, and is paralysed unless the total meets or beats 15 — a 40% chance of resisting
  • Monsters & NPCs: use the exact same DC formula as PCs — there's no separate monster-specific version
  • Monsters Resisting a PC's Spell: a monster targeted by a PC's spell rolls the save printed in its stat block against the caster's DC

Automatic

  • When: used for spells that buff, aid, or produce utility effects with no hostile target, or that strike automatically with no save (e.g. Invisibility, Shield, Bless, Cure Light Wounds, Magic Missile)
  • Resolving: no roll required — the spell simply works

There are no spell attack rolls in Arneyan. Touch spells, ray spells, and ranged spells all use saves if they harm or debuff — there is no separate roll to hit for magic.

A flexible preparation system helps characters adapt to shifting dangers.

  • Preparation: every morning choose a list of spells you have access to. You can prepare a total number of unique spells equal to your Level plus your Ability Modifier (minimum 1)
  • Casting: you have a set number of slots per level. Spend a slot to cast any spell from your prepared list of that same level
  • Bonus slots: a casting stat of 13–15 gives one extra 1st-level slot, 16–17 adds one extra 2nd-level slot, and 18+ adds one extra 3rd-level slot (cumulative). Each arrives only once your class table gives you slots of that level, and you can only prepare or know spells of a level your table gives you slots for. A Bard also knows one extra spell of each of those levels; a Sorcerer gains an extra spell known instead of the slot (see Sorcerer).
  • Casting time: casting a spell takes your action unless the spell says otherwise. A spell takes effect on your turn, but damage taken while you cast it can make you lose it (see Casting Under Threat in The Arneyan Codex).
  • Targeting: you need a clear path to the target or area, and you must be able to see it. A Touch spell needs you to be adjacent, and the target’s save is the dodge: there is no attack roll.
  • Scaling: all spells get stronger automatically as you level up. You can use a higher-level slot to cast a lower-level spell but potency (damage, duration, etc.) is always determined by your caster level (your Class Level in the casting class; for a single-class character, your character level)
  • Changing shape: a spell or feature that changes a creature's form (Polymorph, Shapechange, Wild Shape and similar) gives it the new form's whole stat block from Monsters & Treasure: its HP, AC, attacks, saves and movement. It keeps its own mind, personality and alignment. When the form drops to 0 HP, the creature returns to its own form with the HP it had when it changed; damage beyond 0 does not carry over. The form's Level is capped by the spell or feature.
  • Summoned and conjured attackers: unless a spell or feature says otherwise, you can have only one spell-made attacker at a time (a summoned creature, or the group from one summoning, anything a spell creates that attacks or deals damage on its own each round, such as Spiritual Weapon, Summon Swarm, Animate Objects, Mordenkainen's Sword, Faithful Hound, the Bigby's hands, Shadow Monsters and Changestaff; walls, clouds and areas are not attackers, and familiars and mounts do not count). Casting another ends the first. Summoned creatures act straight after you in the initiative order and obey your spoken commands. Raised undead follow their own control limits instead.
  • Levels: where a spell or ability names a Level ("creatures of Level 4 or lower"), it means a creature's Level in Monsters & Treasure, or a character's level. Hit Dice still set a creature's HP and the totals for raising undead.

Slots, Recovery and Learning Spells

  • Slot recovery: a long rest restores all your spent spell slots. Casters who prepare spells choose their prepared list again after the rest. Cantrips use no slots, so they need no recovery.
  • Reading the tables: in a Spells Per Day table, the 0 column is the number of cantrips you have, cast at will for no slot. Every other column is the number of slots you have of that spell level.
  • Starting spells: a caster who keeps a spellbook (Wizard, Illusionist, Necromancer or Magus) begins with a spellbook holding all their cantrips and six 1st-level spells of their choice from their class list. Clerics, Druids, Paladins and Witches prepare each morning from their whole class list. Bards know a fixed set of spells, as a Sorcerer does: cantrips equal to the 0 column, and for each spell level one more spell than their slots of that level (see the Bard). Cantrips in your 0 column are always known and do not count towards prepared spells.
  • Gaining spells: when a spellbook caster gains a level, they add two spells of a level they can cast to their spellbook for free. Any other spell, from another spellbook or a scroll, is copied at the cost in IX. Casters who need no book learn new spells as their class section describes.

• Spells Requiring a Save: Fireball, Lightning Bolt, Charm Person, Hold Person, Fear, Stinking Cloud, Ray of Enfeeblement, Melf's Acid Arrow, Blindness/Deafness, Bestow Curse, Sleep, Confusion, Dominate Person
  • Automatic Spells (no roll): Magic Missile, Shield, Bless, Invisibility, Cure Light Wounds, Fly, Tongues, Mirror Image, Misty Step

Schools and Traditions

  • Tags: every spell in the Master Spell List carries a tag under its name.
  • Arcane schools: Abjuration (wards and protection), Conjuration (summoning, creation and travel), Divination (knowledge and sight), Enchantment (charm and compulsion), Evocation (raw energy and force), Illusion (false senses), Necromancy (death, life and the undead) and Transmutation (changing the nature of things).
  • Traditions: arcane casters are the Wizard, Illusionist, Necromancer, Sorcerer, Warlock, Witch, Bard and Magus. Divine casters are the Cleric and Paladin. Nature casters are the Druid. A spell on no arcane list is tagged Divine, Nature or both. A spell on an arcane list and on a divine or nature list keeps its arcane school; the Classes column shows everyone who can cast it.
  • School Focus: a Wizard chooses one school at 1st level, and the save DC of that school’s spells is 1 higher.
  • Favoured schools: some arcane casters add every Wizard-list spell of their favoured schools, up to the highest spell level they can cast. Sorcerer: Evocation and Transmutation. Witch: Enchantment, Necromancy and Divination. Bard: Enchantment, Illusion and Divination. Magus: Evocation and Abjuration. Spells your class or kit excludes are never gained this way. Sorcerer: not Time Stop, Forcecage, Limited Wish, Permanency or Polymorph Any Object. Witch: not Power Word Stun, Power Word Blind or Power Word Kill. Magus: not Stoneskin or Melf's Minute Meteors.

Minor magical effects and utility spells are considered Cantrips.

  • Cost: do not consume spell slots
  • Usage: cast at will. Cantrips you know are always prepared and never count against your prepared spells
  • Damaging or Debuffing Cantrips: target makes a save using the standard DC formula above
  • Utility Cantrips: automatic — no roll required

Boss-tier and elite monsters possess Legendary Resistance, replacing spell resistance entirely. Lesser magical creatures may instead have Magic Resistance: Advantage on saves against spells.

  • A monster with Legendary Resistance may automatically succeed on a saving throw a limited number of times per encounter (typically 3, GM discretion)
  • Once all uses are spent the monster must roll saves normally
  • The number of uses and when they are spent is tracked openly — players should know when a boss burns a resistance
  • This applies to saving throws only — it does not negate automatic spells, except that a solo creature may spend a use to ignore a Power Word

Casting requires precise physical focus. Wearing unfamiliar armour disrupts that focus entirely.

  • Spellcasters cannot cast spells while wearing armour they are not trained in
  • If trained in that armour type there is no penalty or restriction — they cast normally
  • Each class lists the armour it is trained in. A class that lists "None" is trained in no armour at all, so wearing any armour or carrying a shield blocks its casting. A shield counts as armour for this rule. The War Caster feat can grant training in one type of Light or Medium armour, or a shield. Only a feat lets a class that lists "None" cast in armour: training from another class, an ancestry or downtime removes the penalties for wearing armour, never the block on casting.
  • This applies to every spellcaster, whatever its class, tradition or ancestry

• Verbal (V): the caster must be able to speak. Silence, a gag, or similar effects stop V spells.
  • Somatic (S): the caster needs at least one free hand. Armour and shields don't matter if the caster is trained in them (see VI).
  • Material (M): a component or focus. Common components are free if you carry a spellcasting focus; a rare component must be acquired before the spell can be cast.
  • Saves: Fortitude = body, poison, death, petrification, sickness. Reflex = dodging blasts and areas. Will = mind, charm, fear, illusion. A — means the spell allows no save. For a reversible (*) spell the Save column shows the save of its harmful form; the normal form allows none. A damage spell with a save deals half damage on a success unless its entry says the save negates.
  • Ritual: a spell tagged Ritual can be cast from your prepared list without spending a slot if you take an extra 10 minutes. Not usable in combat. A spell with its own Ritual text (Wish, Miracle) follows that text instead.
  • Reversible (*): the caster may cast the opposite effect (Cure Light Wounds ↔ Cause Light Wounds) using the same slot.

• Death is not always final. A dying character can still be stabilised (see Death & Dying in The Arneyan Codex); the methods below apply only once the character is dead.
  • Nothing returns a creature whose soul is unwilling (the player decides), trapped (Soul Bind, Trap the Soul, Magic Jar) or raised as undead, or whose spell's time limit or body requirement is not met.
  • Reincarnate (4th, Druid or Witch): dead up to 1 week, needs a body part. Returns in a new random ancestry with 1 HP and 3 levels of Exhaustion. Costs 1,000 gp.
  • Raise Dead (5th, Cleric or Necromancer): dead up to 1 day per level, body intact. Returns with 1 HP and 4 levels of Exhaustion, and permanently loses 1 Constitution. Costs 500 gp.
  • Resurrection (7th, Cleric): dead up to 10 years per level, any piece of the body. Returns with half HP and 2 levels of Exhaustion; no Constitution loss. Costs 1,000 gp.
  • True Resurrection (9th, Cleric): dead up to 200 years per level, no body needed if the name is known. Returns at full HP with no penalty. Costs 25,000 gp.
  • Clone (8th, Wizard, Necromancer or Witch): prepared in advance (5,000 gp, 2d4 months to grow). When the original dies its soul enters the clone with full HP and 2 levels of Exhaustion; no Constitution loss.
  • Wish and Miracle: as a ritual (1 hour; 25,000 gp of components for Wish or 10,000 gp of offerings for Miracle; 2 levels of Exhaustion for the caster), either returns one dead creature as True Resurrection, with no body or time limit.
  • Exhaustion from a return fades as normal (see Fatigue & Exhaustion). A returned character has no spells prepared and keeps its level, class, memories and recovered gear.

Spellbooks

  • Who keeps one: Wizards, Illusionists, Necromancers and Magi. Other casters need no book.
  • Pages: a spellbook (1 slot) holds 100 pages; a spell takes pages equal to its level, a cantrip 1.
  • Preparing: you can only prepare spells from a spellbook you have in hand, or from a copy of it.
  • Copying a spell: from another caster's spellbook or from a scroll, provided the spell is on your class list. It takes 1 day and 50 gp per spell level (the Learn Spells cost), with no roll, and a scroll copied from is used up.
  • Foreign and locked writing: a book in a strange cipher, or one sealed with magic, needs Read Magic before you can copy it.
  • A lost or destroyed book: you keep and cast your prepared spells, but cannot change them until you have a book again. A backup copy costs the same as copying.
  • Hazards: fire, acid or a full hour of immersion ruins a spellbook. Erase can wipe pages.

Scrolls

  • Contents: a scroll holds one spell, and crumbles when it is cast.
  • Who can use one: only a caster of the scroll's tradition (arcane, or divine and nature) can read it; a Bard or Rogue can read an arcane scroll with the unidentified-scroll check. Anyone can use an unread scroll, but its spell is revealed only as it takes effect. Casting needs no slot or components, but you must be able to speak and gesture.
  • Identified scrolls: once Identify (or careful research) has told you what a scroll holds, you can cast it with no check, whatever your class or level.
  • Unidentified scrolls: to read one blind, make a casting-stat check (Intelligence if you have none) against DC 10 + the spell's level. On a failure the scroll is wasted.
  • Potency: a scroll keeps its writer's caster level and save DC. One of unknown origin, or read by someone outside its tradition, casts at caster level 2 × spell level − 1 (minimum 1) and DC 12 + spell level.
  • Writing one: you must know the spell. It takes 1 week and 100 gp per spell level (a cantrip, 1 day and 10 gp) plus costly components, and no more scrolls a month than your casting-stat modifier (minimum 1).
  • Fire and price: exposed scrolls burn easily; a scroll case holds 5. Scrolls of 8th level and above are never sold; the Shopkeeper's Catalogue prices the rest.

Arneyan Master Spell List

All spells available in Arneyan, with the save the target rolls (Fortitude, Reflex or Will; — means automatic, no save), the components needed, and a Ritual tag where a spell can be cast as a ritual. Class-only and Path spells appear in their class chapters; they count as spells of that class for scrolls, Counterspell and Dispel Magic. * = reversible spell. ‡ = needs a costed material component (see Rare Spell Components in the Shopkeeper's Catalogue). Classes listed are those with access in this campaign — Wizard (Wiz), Illusionist (Ill), Cleric (Cle), Druid (Dru), Warlock (War), Sorcerer (Sor), Bard (Bar), Paladin (Pal), Magus (Mag), Necromancer (Nec), Witch (Wit).
Cantrips do not consume spell slots and can be cast at will.
Every spell is in the Spells compendium, sorted by level. Drag a spell onto a character sheet to add it.
